name: DRV8833 dual H-bridge motor driver
description: TI DRV8833 dual H-bridge motor driver with MOSFET bridges: runs two small DC motors (or one bipolar stepper) forwards, backwards, braked or coasting from 3.3 V logic, motor supply 2.7-10.8 V, about 1.2 A per bridge (1 A current limit as fitted). Sold as: Adafruit DRV8833 DC/Stepper Motor Driver Breakout Board (#3297), 8-pin header VM GND FLT BIN1 BIN2 SLP AIN2 AIN1, opposite side AOUT1 AOUT2 BOUT2 BOUT1 AS BS, plus a VMotor screw terminal.
eli5: Lets your board make two small motors spin forwards or backwards, using a battery for the motors' power.

pins.name: VM
pins.description: Motor supply VM, 2.7-10.8 V (also powers the chip; no separate logic supply). Header pin is not reverse-polarity protected; the VMotor screw terminal is

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground: shared by the motor supply and the microcontroller

pins.name: FLT
pins.description: nFAULT output, open-drain: pulled low on overcurrent, overtemperature or undervoltage. Needs a pull-up (e.g. the GPIO's internal one)

pins.name: BIN1
pins.description: Bridge B input 1 (high >= 2 V, max 5.75 V; PWM for speed)

pins.name: SLP
pins.description: nSLEEP: drive high (>= 2.5 V) to run. 500 kOhm pull-down on the chip, so the driver sleeps if this is left open

pins.name: AIN1
pins.description: Bridge A input 1 (high >= 2 V, max 5.75 V; PWM for speed)

pins.name: AOUT1
pins.description: Motor A output 1; connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: AS
pins.description: Bridge A current sense (AISEN): 0.2 Ohm to GND on the board = 1 A limit. Leave unconnected

pins.name: BS
pins.description: Bridge B current sense (BISEN): 0.2 Ohm to GND on the board = 1 A limit. Leave unconnected

buildNotes: Truth table (TI datasheet Table 1): IN1 high/IN2 low = forward, IN1 low/IN2 high = reverse, both high = brake, both low = coast (outputs off).
SLP must be driven high (>= 2.5 V) or the chip stays asleep: it has a 500 kOhm pull-down. Wire it to a GPIO or to 3V3; if you tie it to VM above 6.5 V use a 20-75 kOhm resistor.
Speed: PWM one input. Slow decay (smoother): hold IN1 high and PWM IN2, motor runs while IN2 is low. Fast decay: PWM IN1 with IN2 low.
Motor supply 2.7-10.8 V into the VMotor terminal (reverse-polarity protected) or the VM pin (not protected). Under 5 V the bridge resistance rises and less current is available.
Connect the board GND to the microcontroller GND.
The 0.2 Ohm sense resistors limit each bridge to about 1 A (I = 0.2 V / R). Leave AS/BS unconnected unless you change the limit.
Logic inputs take at most 5.75 V; never connect them to VM.
FLT is open-drain and goes low on a fault; use a pull-up (the GPIO's internal one is enough) if you read it.

driver.code:
# DRV8833 dual H-bridge motor driver (TI DRV8833), MicroPython driver for ONE bridge (one DC motor).
# Make one DRV8833 object per motor: bridge A = AIN1, AIN2; bridge B = BIN1, BIN2.
# H-bridge logic from the TI datasheet (SLVSAR1E, Table 1):
#   xIN1 = 0, xIN2 = 0 -> outputs Hi-Z: coast / fast decay
#   xIN1 = 0, xIN2 = 1 -> reverse
#   xIN1 = 1, xIN2 = 0 -> forward
#   xIN1 = 1, xIN2 = 1 -> brake / slow decay
# Speed control (Table 2), slow decay: forward = xIN1 high + PWM on xIN2, reverse = PWM on xIN1 + xIN2 high.
# In slow decay the motor is driven while the PWM pin is LOW, so the PWM duty is (100 - speed) %.
# Inputs: high >= 2 V, low <= 0.7 V, max 5.75 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs work. nSLEEP (SLP) needs >= 2.5 V and
# has a 500 kOhm pull-down: the chip sleeps (outputs off) until SLP is driven high; it needs up to 1 ms to wake.
from machine import Pin, PWM
import time


class DRV8833:
    def __init__(self, in1, in2, slp=None, freq=20000):
        """in1, in2: GPIO numbers of the bridge's inputs (AIN1/AIN2 or BIN1/BIN2).
        slp: GPIO number wired to SLP (nSLEEP), or None if SLP is tied high elsewhere.
        freq: PWM frequency for speed control (20 kHz is above hearing)."""
        self._n1 = in1
        self._n2 = in2
        self._freq = freq
        self._pwm = None
        self.a = Pin(in1, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.b = Pin(in2, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.slp = None
        if slp is not None:
            self.slp = Pin(slp, Pin.OUT, value=0)
            self.wake()

    def wake(self):
        """Drive nSLEEP high and wait the 1 ms start-up time (tWAKE)."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    def sleep(self):
        """nSLEEP low: H-bridges off, about 1.6 uA from VM. Shared by both bridges on the board."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(0)

    def _digital(self, v1, v2):
        if self._pwm is not None:
            self._pwm.deinit()
            self._pwm = None
            self.a = Pin(self._n1, Pin.OUT)
            self.b = Pin(self._n2, Pin.OUT)
        self.a.value(v1)
        self.b.value(v2)

    def _slow_decay(self, high_pin, pwm_pin, speed):
        # high_pin held at 1, pwm_pin low for `speed` % of each period (driving), high otherwise (braking).
        speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
        if speed >= 100:
            return False
        if self._pwm is not None:
            self._pwm.deinit()
            self._pwm = None
        Pin(high_pin, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self._pwm = PWM(Pin(pwm_pin), freq=self._freq, duty_u16=(100 - speed) * 65535 // 100)
        return True

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """Spin one way (xOUT1 high, xOUT2 low). speed 0-100 %."""
        if not self._slow_decay(self._n1, self._n2, speed):
            self._digital(1, 0)

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """Spin the other way (xOUT1 low, xOUT2 high). speed 0-100 %."""
        if not self._slow_decay(self._n2, self._n1, speed):
            self._digital(0, 1)

    def brake(self):
        """Both inputs high: both outputs low, the motor is shorted and stops quickly."""
        self._digital(1, 1)

    def coast(self):
        """Both inputs low: outputs Hi-Z, the motor spins down freely."""
        self._digital(0, 0)

    def stop(self):
        self.brake()


def fault(pin_no):
    """True while FLT (nFAULT, open-drain, low on overcurrent/overtemperature/undervoltage) is asserted.
    Uses the GPIO's internal pull-up; the Adafruit board has no pull-up on FLT."""
    return Pin(pin_no, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP).value() == 0

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from drv8833 import DRV8833

# Motor A on AIN1/AIN2; SLP driven high by the driver to wake the chip.
motor = DRV8833({AIN1}, {AIN2}, slp={SLP})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor A forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.coast()
    print('motor A coasting')
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Wakes the driver, runs motor A forward, then lets it coast
